title: What kind of item skips committee
question: What sort of business goes through on the calendar that needs no committee hearing, and how much money does it name?
finding: 68% of the 1,734 files adopted without committee reference are commemorations, positions on bills, appointments to advisory bodies or the Board’s own meeting business. 67 are money items, 8 of them naming $100,000 or more ($3.47 billion in all, most of it one bond authorisation shown in the next screen). The largest groups: positions (550); commemorations (381); land-use steps (331); meeting business (138).
how: Each file adopted without committee reference is sorted by its short title, first match winning, in this order: meeting business, emergencies, money items (a dollar figure, or the words grant, bond, agreement, contract, appropriation, lease, loan, settlement or fee), appointments, land-use steps, positions, commemorations. Dollars are the largest figure printed in the short title; a title that only schedules a hearing about a sum is counted with the sum it names.
limits: The sorting is by title wording and is rough at the edges; the example column shows a real title from each group. A dollar figure in a title is not always money approved: several of these files schedule a hearing, support a State bill that carries a sum, or apply for a grant rather than accept one. That the calendar is mostly ceremonial is the reassuring reading, and it is what the count shows. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).

rows.kind: Positions: urging, supporting or opposing a bill or policy
rows.example: Opposing California State Assembly Bill No. 2063 (Berman) - Expanded State Density Bonus Law - Unless Amended

rows.kind: Commemorations: days, weeks, months and commendations
Land-use steps: landmark initiations, review extensions, findings on appeals, street and sidewalk matters
Meeting business: hearings of the whole Board, closed sessions, schedules, rules, ballot arguments
rows.example: Committee of the Whole - Loan Agreement - Metropolitan Transportation Commission - Public Transit Operating Purposes - $200,000,000 - June 1
Resolution of Intent to Designate the Wild Parrots of San Francisco as the Official Animal of San Francisco

rows.kind: Emergencies: concurring in emergency actions and remote-meeting findings
rows.example: Emergency Declaration - Portsmouth Square Elevators Modernization - Cost of Repairs Not to Exceed $2,200,000

rows.kind: Money items: grants, bonds, agreements, appropriations, settlements and fee waivers
rows.example: Issuance of Revenue Bonds - Public Utilities Commission - Purchase of Electricity Distribution and Transmission System - Not to Exceed $3,06

sources.t: San Francisco Board of Supervisors: legislation records with titles, dates and action history (Legistar; each row links to its file)
